title: The Final Hand
description:
Less than a year left until 38. You chose to go all-in.
Today a tip came in. A broker you know.
'This is the last window. Double up or nothing.'
Gangnam comes down to this one decision.

choices.result_text: I pushed all my chips in. There was no turning back now.

You stepped back.
Aggressive all the way through — but the finish line, you take with what you have.
The broker called you a coward. You hung up.
The number in your account isn't wrong.

title: What You Protected
description:
You spent the final year protecting what you had.
Today the full portfolio valuation came up.
Five years ago you started with ₩500,000.
You stared at the number for a long time.

choices.result_text:
Not losing was the strategy.
You watched others shoot up on a single bet, then collapse.
This number was built without flinching.
Gangnam is secondary. Becoming this person — that came first.

choices.text: One more — since it's the end
choices.result_text: I couldn't remember how many times I'd called it the last time.

title: On the Finish Line
description:
It's been months since you wondered if Gangnam is even the goal.
Today you sat on a Han River bench doing nothing.
Your phone buzzed. It's Daeun.
Or Dad. Or just an ad.

choices.result_text:
It was Daeun. 'Free tonight?'
Instead of calculating apartment square footage, you replied.
'Yes.'
Whether Gangnam is the goal — you'll think about that over dinner.

choices.text: Pocket the phone and look at the river
choices.result_text:
The Han River flowed.
Five years flowed.
What you ran all this way for — right now it seems clearer.
The finish line is yours to define.

title: The Tilt Invoice
description:
After the bad beat tilt-shove you lost ₩150,000 more.
On the subway home, you ran the numbers.
Total loss today: ₩230,000.
Half of next month's goshiwon rent.

choices.text: Make a rule: tilt means leave
choices.result_text:
You wrote it in your phone notes. 'Tilt = walk out.'
The moment emotion enters, the judgment is already wrong.
Poker taught you something that works outside poker too.

That's what you told yourself.
But the person who says 'I'll win next time' is exactly the one who tilts again.
Knowing doesn't make it stop.

title: The Private Game
description:
After the big win at the table, the dealer approached separately.
'If you're interested — there's a separate game.
Much higher stakes, higher level.
About ten times tonight.'

choices.result_text: It was a basement in some building in Gangnam. Every face gathered at the table was a stranger's.

'I'll pass.'
The dealer said 'Shame.'
You pocketed tonight's winnings.
Knowing your level is a skill.

title: News from the Table
description:
A month since you quit the holdem pub.
Today a KakaoTalk from someone who used to sit at the same table.
'Hey, remember me? We played together.
I lost everything yesterday. ₩800,000.'

choices.text: "That was the right call. For real."
choices.result_text:
'I think leaving was right for me too.'
Couldn't tell if you were saying it for them or for yourself.
Leaving was right.

Replied 'Hang in there.'
Somebody collapsed in the seat you'd vacated.
Leaving was right.

title: Six Months After the Switch
description:
Six months since switching to the startup.
Salary went up. But something like burnout is starting.
The co-founder asked. 'How is it? Glad you came?'

choices.text: "I think so. I'm learning a lot."
choices.result_text:
50% genuine, 50% survival mode.
But actually learning more than a year at the old job would've taught.
The switch was right.

The co-founder laughed. 'Everyone says that at six months.'
Somehow reassuring and not reassuring at once.
Decided to keep going anyway.

title: That Startup's News
description:
Five months since turning down the offer.
A news article appeared on the portal today.
[OO Startup Successfully Raises ₩8 Billion Series B]
The colleague who tried to bring you along is in the article.

choices.text: Close the article. Regret doesn't help.
choices.result_text:
You closed it.
Hindsight. It could have failed.
You have a steady paycheck coming in every month.
Whether this was the right call — still unknown.

'Saw the article. Congrats.'
They replied 'Thanks. You should've come.'
'I know.' That's all you said.
The connection stayed alive.

title: Position Filled
description:
'Give me a few days to think.' That startup.
You spent the time pulling apart the financials.
Today a text from the colleague.
'Hey, sorry. That role went to someone else yesterday.'

choices.result_text:
'Yeah. Nothing to do about it.'
You analyzed it thoroughly and still came too late.
Careful doesn't always mean safe. Opportunities have expiry dates.

Colleague said 'I'll look around.'
This time you decided to cut the conditions-checking shorter.
There's no perfect timing.

title: Loan Declined
description:
An investment opportunity came up. You went to the bank.
The loan officer looked at the screen and their expression stiffened.
'Your credit rating is below grade 7.
We can't offer this at a Tier 1 bank.'

choices.result_text:
Got advice from a credit specialist.
'Keep it clean for six months and your grade goes up.'
Six months. Can't get it now.
But there's a path.

Got it at a Tier 2 bank. Monthly rate 1.6%.
Twice the Tier 1 rate.
Got the money. But the interest calculation was frightening.

title: The Value of a Line
description:
Two months since you told your boss 'Put my name on it next time.'
The new report went up today.
Two names in the title. The boss. And {name}.

choices.result_text:
The boss didn't say anything special.
But the name was there.
The person who drew the line gets to keep the line.

'Thank you. Please keep working with me.'
Boss said 'Yeah, keep it up.'
Awkward — but it's the right direction.

title: Day 30
description:
A month since you admitted 'Something's off with me lately.'
App usage time is under half of two months ago.
Last night you fell asleep before 11 PM for the first time.

choices.result_text:
Wrote it down. 'Day 30. Better than before.'
Not completely clean. But watching it.
Admitting it was step one. Step one happened.

Moving carefully.
You know complacency is the most dangerous thing.
Not complete yet.

title: Temptation
description:
You recorded 21 days of no betting apps.
Today a friend texted.
'Hey, watching the game tonight? There's a 3.2x line.
Really certain. Just this once.'

choices.text: "I'm quitting right now. Don't even bring it up."
choices.result_text:
Said it honestly for the first time.
Friend said 'Oh sorry, I didn't know.'
21 days held.
Saying it out loud is how you keep it.

'Just once' became twice.
21 days reset.
Back to day one.
Harder now. Because you know what a reset feels like.

title: Words from That Night
description:
A drunk man at the night shift said something.
'Did I endure it? No. I just got up the next day.'
This morning you didn't want to get up and were lying there — and suddenly those words came back.

choices.result_text:
You got up.
No special reason.
Just got up the next day.
That seems to be how you get through it.

Ten minutes became thirty.
But you got up eventually.
That drunk man probably did the same thing.

title: Visiting Home
description:
Eight months since you saw the number in your parents' bankbook.
You came back to the hometown today for the first time in a while.
Dad was sitting at the dining table. He'd set out dinner.
That number came back to mind.

choices.result_text:
Left ₩200,000.
Dad said 'It's fine' but didn't refuse it.
On the bus back, something felt lighter than it should have.

You ate.
Dad said 'Come more often.'
You can't give much right now —
but this time, you could give.

title: -15% from the Peak
description:
'The ceiling isn't here yet' — and you held.
Kept it too long past the peak.
Today you cut the position and ran the numbers.
Difference between what you sold vs. what you got: ₩8.2 million.

choices.text: Set a profit target rule going forward
choices.result_text:
Made the rule. '+40% — sell half.'
₩8.2 million is the tuition for greed.
Expensive — but some people pay more.

choices.text: Nothing to do. Find the next opportunity.
choices.result_text:
A gain is still a gain.
It ended in profit, not at -₩8.2M.
But that number is going to sit in the back of the mind for a while.

title: The Cost of Honesty
description:
Two months since you told your team lead 'I didn't actually have that experience.'
Today the team lead called you in.
'{name}, do you know what happened with the presentation?'

choices.result_text:
'Thank you for being honest.
I reviewed the presentation content myself. It wasn't bad.
We're letting this one go. Next time — be honest from the start.'
The team lead left.
Honesty wasn't the end.

title: Caught
description:
You pulled off the presentation after studying through the night. You submitted the altered transcript too.
Today the team lead called you in.
'{name}. We verified the original transcript directly with your university.'

choices.result_text:
'...I'm sorry. Everything I did was wrong.'
Team lead said 'You're suspended as of today. HR will contact you.' 
The walk back was long.
If you'd been honest from the start, it wouldn't have come to this.

'Are you sure you checked the right person?'
The team lead's expression went flat.
'It's the original. Please leave.'
The lie on top of the forgery. Two layers now.
